x.t: Indian scientists make a vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu
b: Scientists in [[bhopal|Bhopal]], India, have made a new [[vaccine|vaccine]] for chickens. It protects them from bird flu. It is the first bird flu vaccine for chickens made in India.
A vaccine teaches the body to fight a germ before it arrives. Animals can get vaccines too, just like people.
Each dose may cost only one or two rupees. That could help chicken farmers keep their birds healthy.

o.t: India launches its first homegrown bird flu vaccine for chickens
b: India's first indigenous, or homegrown, [[vaccine|vaccine]] against H5N1 bird flu in chickens was launched in [[bhopal|Bhopal]] last week by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. It was developed by the [[icar-nihsad|ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases]] (NIHSAD) in Bhopal.

A vaccine trains the body to recognise a germ and fight it before it can cause illness. H5N1 is a type of bird flu [[virus|virus]], a tiny germ that can make living things sick. India has had more than 500 bird flu outbreaks, or sudden spreads of the illness, since 2006.

Each dose is expected to cost about Rs 1 to Rs 2. A low price matters because [[poultry|poultry]] farmers, who raise chickens and other birds, may need to protect many birds at once. The new vaccine gives them a homegrown way to do that.

stories.think: Why do you think it helps to protect animals from an illness before it arrives, instead of waiting until they are sick?

quiz.q: About how much is each dose of the new chicken vaccine expected to cost?

x.t: China's space station is getting its first visitor from abroad
b: China has a space station called [[tiangong|Tiangong]]. It is a science lab that goes [[orbit|around Earth]]. Soon it should get its first visitor from another country.
The visitor will be an astronaut from Pakistan. Pakistan has picked two people. One will fly. The other will be a backup.
A rocket is ready at the launch site. Workers have practised the launch. The visitor should stay about a week.

o.t: China's Tiangong station set to welcome its first foreign astronaut
b: China's space station, [[tiangong|Tiangong]], is expected to host its first visitor from another country: an astronaut from Pakistan. A space station is a laboratory in [[orbit|orbit]], the curved path an object follows around a planet, where astronauts live and do experiments.

On 17 November, a Long March 2F rocket and the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft were moved to the launch area at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. On Sunday, a launch rehearsal, or full practice, was reported complete. China has not officially announced the launch date, but SpacePolicyOnline, a space news website, reports it is planned for 25 November.

The mission is set to carry three astronauts. Pakistan has two candidates, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud. One will fly as a [[payload-specialist|payload specialist]], a crew member who carries out science work, and the other is the backup. The astronaut chosen is expected to stay about a week and return to Earth aboard a different spacecraft, Shenzhou-23.

stories.think: If you could do one science experiment on a space station, what would you test, and why?

quiz.q: How long is the Pakistani astronaut expected to stay on Tiangong?

x.t: Carlos Alcaraz wins the ATP Finals for the first time
b: Carlos Alcaraz has won a big tennis event called the [[atp-finals|ATP Finals]]. Only the season's top players get to play in it.
In the final, he beat Alexander Zverev in Turin, Italy. Zverev was the world number one player.
Alcaraz came close to losing the [[set|second set]] three times. He stayed calm and won it. It is the 30th title of his career.

o.t: Alcaraz saves three set points to win his first ATP Finals title
b: Carlos Alcaraz won the [[atp-finals|ATP Finals]], the season-ending event for the year's top men's players, for the first time on Sunday 22 November. In the final in Turin, Italy, he beat Alexander Zverev, who went into the match as world No. 1, by 6-2, 7-6.

Tennis matches are split into [[set|sets]], groups of games. The second set went to a [[tie-break|tie-break]], a special game played to decide a close set. Zverev had three set points, chances to win the set, but Alcaraz stayed calm, saved them all and won the tie-break 9-7.

It is the 30th title of Alcaraz's career and his sixth of 2026. He is now one of only four men, with Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, to have won all four Grand Slam [[tournament|tournaments]], the sport's biggest events, and the ATP Finals.

stories.think: What helps you stay calm when something is very close to going wrong?

quiz.q: How many set points did Alcaraz save in the second-set tie-break?

x.t: India's women's hockey team wins 7-0 and reaches the semi-finals
b: India's women's hockey team beat Thailand 7-0 on Sunday. The match was in Bhopal, India.
A player called Deepika scored three goals. That is called a [[hat-trick|hat-trick]]. Navneet Kaur scored two goals.
India has won all three of its games. Now it is in the semi-finals of the [[asian-champions-trophy|Asian Champions Trophy]]. Semi-final winners play in the final.

o.t: India beat Thailand 7-0 to reach Asian Champions Trophy semi-finals
b: India's women's hockey team beat Thailand 7-0 on Sunday 22 November to seal a place in the semi-finals of the Women's [[asian-champions-trophy|Asian Champions Trophy]]. The [[tournament|tournament]] is being played in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, from 19 to 28 November.

Deepika scored a [[hat-trick|hat-trick]], three goals in one match. Navneet Kaur scored twice from [[penalty-stroke|penalty strokes]], free shots at goal with only the goalkeeper defending. Mumtaz Khan and Sunelita Toppo also scored.

It was India's third win from three matches. Led by captain Salima Tete, the team had already beaten Malaysia 4-1 on 19 November and South Korea 2-1 on 21 November. A semi-final is the round before the final, so India are now two wins away from the title.

stories.think: What do you think helps a team keep winning game after game?

x.t: BepiColombo is safe at Mercury after a computer problem
b: On Saturday, the spacecraft BepiColombo started going around [[mercury|Mercury]]. But one part did not go to plan.
Its engines fired to slow it down. A problem with its [[software|computer program]] stopped them early. The [[esa|European Space Agency]] says the spacecraft is safe.
Teams on Earth are working out what happened. They can check on it from very far away. Updates are due today.

o.t: BepiColombo safe in Mercury orbit after software glitch
b: BepiColombo, a joint mission of the [[esa|European Space Agency]] (ESA) and JAXA, Japan's space agency, went into [[orbit|orbit]] around [[mercury|Mercury]] on Saturday 21 November. It launched in 2018 and took about eight years to get there. But ESA said the engine burn, a firing of its engines to slow it down, was shorter than planned following a [[software|software]] issue. Software is the set of instructions that tells a computer what to do.

ESA said: "The spacecraft is safe." Teams at ESOC, the European Space Operations Centre, are working to understand what happened. ESOC is ESA's mission control, where people guide spacecraft from Earth.

ESA promised updates today, Monday 23 November. BepiColombo carries two orbiters, or spacecraft built to circle a planet: ESA's MPO and JAXA's Mio. They are due to separate around 9 December. Science work is due to start in April 2027.

stories.think: When something you planned goes wrong, what steps do you take to work out what happened?

quiz.q: What made BepiColombo's engine burn end early?

days.name: Fibonacci Day
days.what: Fibonacci Day honours Leonardo of Pisa, known as Fibonacci, and the number pattern named after him. In the Fibonacci sequence, each number is the sum of the two before it: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on. Written month first, the date 11/23 shows 1, 1, 2, 3. Fibonacci described the sequence in 1202 and helped spread Hindu-Arabic numerals in Europe.

learn.subject: Science
learn.link: From the bird flu vaccine story: a vaccine helps a body learn to protect itself

x.t: How a vaccine trains the body
b: Some germs can make people and animals ill. India has made a new vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu.
A vaccine has germs that are made weak or switched off. Some vaccines have just a small part of a germ. These do not make you ill.
The body learns to spot the germ. It makes antibodies, tiny helpers that fight the germ. It also remembers the germ, so it can act fast next time.
x.remember: A vaccine teaches the body to spot a germ, so it is ready to fight it next time.
x.q: What does a vaccine teach the body to do?
a: Spot a germ and fight it

o.t: How does a vaccine train the body to protect itself?
b: A vaccine helps the body get ready for a germ before it meets the real thing. Most vaccines contain a weakened or inactive form of a germ, such as a virus or bacterium, or a small part of one. This part is called an antigen: something the body's defences can recognise. Some newer vaccines carry instructions that let the body make the antigen itself.

The immune system is the body's defence system. Its immune cells make antibodies, which are proteins that recognise a particular antigen and help fight it. The first time the body meets an antigen, it needs time to make the right antibodies. A vaccine lets this happen without the dangers of a real illness.

Afterwards, the immune system keeps a memory of the germ. If the real germ arrives later, the body can make the right antibodies quickly. Vaccines are used for animals as well as people: India's new bird flu vaccine is meant to protect chickens.
o.remember: A vaccine shows the immune system a harmless form of a germ, so it can remember the germ and respond quickly later.
o.q: What happens if the real germ arrives after a vaccine has done its work?
a: The body makes the right antibodies quickly
The vaccine turns into the germ

backThen.t: Doctor Who is shown on television for the first time
backThen.o: On 23 November 1963, the BBC showed the first episode of Doctor Who on television in the United Kingdom. The episode was called An Unearthly Child. The programme was cancelled in 1989, but it came back in 2005.
backThen.x: On this day in 1963, the first episode of Doctor Who was shown on TV in the UK. The BBC made it. The show stopped in 1989. It came back in 2005.
backThen.why: A television programme can stop and still return: Doctor Who came back in 2005, 16 years after it was cancelled.

hiddenWords.o: Orbit comes from the Latin word orbita, which means a wheel track or path. The Romans also used it for the path of a heavenly body through the sky.
Tournament comes from the Old French word torneiement, which became tornement in Middle English. It meant a contest between two teams of knights on horseback.
